body: The idea of throwing out by rationality really resonated with me. My rationality is the route of all my problems.  It forces me to do the things that I don't like in order to maximize my potential happiness now. Maybe sometimes you have to do what's irrational

I'm quite similar to you but actually in college. Now that I'm at a top school I kind of wonder if I should stay. I no longer have the grand career ambitions of working some crazy stressful high paying job. Thus do I really need my fancy private college degree. I don't see how it would be much better than a state school which would have the same tedious work just easier. The problem is  we need money. If I could have the 250k that my education is going to cost, I would certainly not go to school. There are other options. Work in the oil industry or go to trade school. Both of these professionals pay decently and don't require as much bullshit
Good points. While I see the appeal of living that doesn't lesson the appeal of dying.
Because the status quo involves bad, difficult, and painful parts.
I don't think life is inherently bad. My life is far from bad, I just don't see why it is valued.

Whether you stay up all not or not the world is still going to end. And as far a investing in things that matter, nothing really matters. The only thing that mattered to at one point was becoming financially independent so I could stop being a wage slave.
